A_target.statement:
Let $0 \to A \xrightarrow f B \xrightarrow g C \to 0$ be a [[Definition:Short Exact Sequence|short exact sequence]] of [[Definition:Module|modules]].
Then:
:$\Img f = \map \ker g$, $A \cong \Img f$, and $C \cong B / \Img f$

B_source.statement:
Let $g: B \to C$ be a [[Definition:Module Homomorphism|homomorphism]].
Then:
:$B / \map \ker g \cong \Img g$

substitutions.the single map f: B -> C: a chain of maps A -> B -> C
substitutions.im(f): C when B -> C is surjective

derived.B/ker(f) ~= im(f): B/A ~= C (when the sequence is exact)
derived.one isomorphism theorem: a packaging of sub/quotient relationships along a chain

object_map.reformulation: Reframe the kernel-image equality of a single homomorphism as an exactness condition (im = ker) at each spot of a chain of maps.

validity_conditions: Exactness at B means im(A->B) = ker(B->C); with injectivity of A->B and surjectivity of B->C this recovers A ~= subobject and C ~= B/A.
The first iso theorem is the single-map special case; generalizing to chains adds genuine structure (the sequence), so this is generalization, not transport.
proof_plan:
Start from the [[First Isomorphism Theorem for Modules]] for $g$:
:$B / \map \ker g \cong \Img g$
Encode $\map \ker g$ as the image of an incoming map $f: A \to B$, and $\Img g$ as the codomain of a [[Definition:Surjection|surjection]] $g: B \to C$.

[[Definition:Exact Sequence|Exactness]] at $A$ means $f$ is [[Definition:Injection|injective]], at $C$ that $g$ is surjective, and at $B$ that:
:$\Img f = \map \ker g$
